target.","requiredFixes":[{"rubricItem":"resolver","severity":"warning","summary":"Resolution rule adds ambiguity by allowing revision if the registered snapshot is replaced before capture, while the target contract is a registered-query snapshot with first-print treatment tied to the 2026-10-22 resolution date.","actionRequested":"Restate the rule as resolving to the captured registered-query snapshot for the exact agency 097 endpoint on 2026-10-22, contracts row aggregated_amount times 1e-9, with no later restatements or same-day corrections unless the registration protocol itself defines recapture."},{"rubricItem":"update","severity":"warning","summary":"The point estimate moves from a 450B persistence prior to 485B, but the draft does not use or explicitly rule out current FY2026 time, or explicitly state why the live partial API value was not used and why budget evidence alone supports the +35B update."},{"rubricItem":"interval","severity":"warning","summary":"The interval is based on final FY2015-FY2024 CRS/FPDS volatility, not volatility of the registered USAspending first-snapshot measurement with DoD reporting lag.","actionRequested":"Either justify final FPDS volatility as a proxy for the first-snapshot USAspending target, or widen/adjust the interval to account for API first-print lag and source-definition mismatch."}],"optionalSuggestions":["Clarify whether CRS history excludes categories that USAspending's contracts row may include or omit, since the draft notes the proxy mismatch but does not quantify it.","Name the exact historical sample source for FY2015-FY2019 values used in sigma, because only FY2020-FY2024 values appear in historicalContext.","Make the downside tail explicitly include an unusually incomplete Oct. 22 DoD reporting snapshot, not only lower underlying obligations."]}
